changes.reason: a YAML path that starts with a stashed value ($profile.uid) is read inside that value; upstream reads the stashed value as a key of the response, which finds nothing, so the generated test failed on every server, Elasticsearch included; no other generated test changes

it created x_pack_rest_user, the superuser some x-pack tests authenticate as, in the native realm on every cluster; Elastic's test clusters define that user in the file realm, as elasticsearch-8-security does, and a test that lists native users (TestXpack_SecurityUserProfile) counted the extra one; the setup now creates it only where it cannot authenticate as it, so on a cluster without the file user the setup is upstream's

changes.what: the order the generator writes a request's fields and headers in (internal/build/cmd/generate/commands/gentests)
changes.reason: it walked them as Go maps, so two generations of the same YAML differed, and our record of which call each test line checks could disagree with the built tests; they are now sorted, which changes no request a test sends

changes.what: YAML tests the generated client cannot express
changes.reason: the generator runs with --skip-on-error, which leaves such a test out of the generated tests instead of failing the build; on every target alike

changes.what: the client's product check (elasticsearch.go: Config.SkipProductCheck, set by the generated tests' client setup in internal/build/cmd/generate/commands/gentests/generator.go)
changes.reason: a conforming client refuses a server that does not send X-Elastic-Product: Elasticsearch, so the YAML tests measured nothing on an Elasticsearch-compatible server without it; the option is off unless ELASTICSEARCH_SKIP_PRODUCT_CHECK is set, so the stock client and the stock measurement are unchanged
